note: Source pool is the 65 entries for comune di Roma in the MASAF national register, cross-read against the Lazio regional register (https://www.regione.lazio.it/sites/default/files/2025-11/Elenco-alberi-monumentali.xlsx, Nov 2025), which is the richer of the two: it carries the monumentality criteria per tree, a NOTE column, and a second sheet of trees REMOVED from the list with the reason. Six trees were published from this pass as rom_011 to rom_016, thickening the Villa Sciarra, Trastevere, Capitoline and Villa Borghese walks. Everything else is here. Do not quote 65 as a count of monumental trees in Rome: it is a count of register entries, six of them are 'insieme omogeneo' groups rather than single trees, and 22 of them stand inside a closed presidential estate. Rome's own municipal page NWS1195295 narrates only about 20 of them, the batch registered up to 2018; sheets numbered 57 and above have no municipal narrative at all, which is why several entries below are stuck at one source.

leads.name: Stone Pine of Villa Torlonia
leads.why_not_published: Second tallest tree on Rome's register and a textbook umbrella pine, but register-only: sheet 75 postdates the municipal narrative page. Note that a different Villa Torlonia stone pine, sheet 18, is on the Lazio REMOVED list as dead, so any pass shipping this one must be explicit about which is which. VITALITY RISK RAISED, 2026-08-08 (rom deepen verify pass): press coverage found this pass shows Villa Torlonia's whole tree stock under active safety felling. Il Messaggero/La Capitale (11 Dec 2025) report 19 trees felled after a stability survey rated them 'classe di cedimento D' (highest risk), including 4 Pinus pinea; RomaToday/La Capitale describe further urgent fellings continuing into 2026 (5 more trees in March 2026, though that batch was palms, an Aleppo pine and a Judas tree, not stone pines). None of the coverage found names which specific stone pines were among the 4 felled in December. The Lazio Nov 2025 xlsx (which is our source for this lead) still listed sheet 75 as active, i.e. before the December felling, so the register cannot settle this either way. Given the confirmed sibling already dead (sheet 18) and 4 more stone pines felled in the same park weeks after our register snapshot, this tree should NOT ship without a specific, dated confirmation that sheet 75 itself is still standing. Not blocked (not confirmed dead), but do not verify from the register alone; needs a targeted post-December-2025 check, ideally the Lazio register's next update or a dated photo/observation.

leads.name: Mediterranean Hackberry of the Mura Latine
leads.why_not_published: Register-only. Larger of the pair, registered for size and for particular form and bearing, standing against the Aurelian wall at the corner of Via Latina. CHECKED AGAIN 2026-08-08 (rom deepen verify pass): its twin 120m away (sheet 66, Parco degli Scipioni) now has a second source and shipped as rom_024; this one still does not. The Parco Regionale dell'Appia Antica's own 'alberi di pregio' catalogue (parcoappiaantica.it/il-territorio/alberi-di-pregio-appia-antica/), which independently corroborated the Scipioni tree, lists 13 named trees of value across the whole regional park and does not include a second bagolaro at the Mura Latine/Via Latina corner. RAMI (ilregistrodeglialberi.it) site search returns no matching entry. Genuinely still register-only; do not fold it into rom_024 as a pair since only one of the two is independently corroborated, and folding would overstate what is known about this one.

leads.name: Mexican Blue Palm of Villa Sciarra
leads.why_not_published: Register-only, listed for botanical rarity alone. Would make Villa Sciarra a four-tree walk with rom_001, rom_011 and rom_012. Needs one independent source naming this individual palm; general descriptions of the villa's palms are not enough to fix which one. CHECKED AGAIN 2026-08-08 (rom deepen verify pass): comune.roma.it's own monumental-tree narrative page (NWS1195295) covers Villa Sciarra's Ginkgo and Podocarpus but names no palm there; general Brahea armata gardening pages and the Villa Sciarra Wikipedia disambiguation page have nothing on this specific tree. Still a dead end on the second-source hunt.

leads.name: Pino dell'Himalaya (second Chir Pine), sheet 70
leads.why_not_published: NEW, spotted 2026-08-08 (rom deepen verify pass) while cross-checking the register against published pins; not previously in this leads file and not part of this pass's briefed candidate list, so left entirely unresearched. Distinct from the published Chir Pine of Colle Oppio (rom_020, sheet 71/H501/RM/12, 41.893528,12.497111): this is a second, separate Pinus roxburghii roughly 2.7km further east/southeast, near no currently published cluster. Needs a from-scratch look: what site it stands on, whether public, and a second source.

leads.name: Black Poplar of Via Conca d'Oro
leads.why_not_published: Register-only, street corner in Montesacro, no cluster. Black poplars are short-lived and split; vitality would need checking before any pass.

leads.name: Plane of Viale Jonio
leads.why_not_published: Two sources, clears the bar, but it is a street-corner tree in Montesacro 6km out with nothing near it. Second thickest plane on the register after our rom_013.

leads.name: Black Poplar of the Risaro
leads.why_not_published: Third thickest trunk on the Roma register, but the Lazio register's own NOTE says it was burned in a fire in 2025 and asserts its monumental character is unaffected. That is the register's judgement of a tree that caught fire eight months ago, not a vitality check. Far south of the city besides. Needs eyes before it can ever ship.

leads.name: Holm Oak of Ostia Antica
leads.why_not_published: Register-only. Piazza della Rocca at Ostia Antica, registered for size and for historical value. Roughly 40 minutes by train from the centre, so it fails the 30-minute day-trip boundary for a Rome page and belongs to an Ostia page if one is ever made.

leads.name: Almonds of the Villa di Faonte
leads.why_not_published: Two registered almonds 90m apart at Via delle Vigne Nuove 280, an address attached to the so-called Villa di Faonte. Register-only, access unverified, and a monumental almond would be a genuine curiosity, so worth checking whether the grounds are public before writing it off. Real February blossom peak if it ever ships. CHECKED 2026-08-08 (rom deepen verify pass): RomaToday reports the Villa di Faonte archaeological park itself reopened to the public after ten years closed ('Villa di Faonte, dopo dieci anni apre il parco: restano sbarrati i casali'), access from Via delle Vigne Nuove and Via del Passo del Turchino, which is encouraging on general access but does not confirm the two specific almond trees are inside the reopened area rather than on an adjacent closed plot, and no second source names the trees themselves. Still needs a dedicated look, not part of this pass's briefed cluster.

leads.name: Plane of the Galoppatoio
sources: https://www.carteinregola.it/o-adesso-o-mai-piu-gli-amici-di-villa-borghese-scrivono-allassessora/ (mentions a deteriorating plane at the Galoppatoio)
leads.why_not_published: 2026-08-07 verify pass (rom deepen, Villa Borghese cluster). The Amici di Villa Borghese letter names a plane tree at the former Galoppatoio (the old riding ground, now closed and under redevelopment) as declining, but web search turned up a confusing second thread about newly planted trees at the same site being 'dead on their feet' per municipal agronomists, per il Caffe di Roma and Il Messaggero coverage of the Galoppatoio's 2024 closure and sequester. Could not establish within this pass's window whether the 'deteriorating plane' the letter means is an old historic specimen or one of the recent plantings, nor pin coordinates. Vitality and identity both unresolved; needs a dedicated look, not a padded guess.

leads.name: Holm oaks of Viale delle Due Piramidi
sources: https://www.carteinregola.it/o-adesso-o-mai-piu-gli-amici-di-villa-borghese-scrivono-allassessora/ ('lecci cinquecenteschi lungo Viale delle Due Piramidi')
leads.why_not_published: 2026-08-07 verify pass. Described only as an avenue of 16th-century holm oaks, not a named individual; likely not a collectible point (an avenue, like the Valle dei Platani group) unless a single standout specimen can be identified. Left as a lead in case a future pass finds one tree singled out.

leads.name: Holm oaks of the Parco dei Daini
sources: roma2pass.it/villa-borghese/alberi/ ('Nel Parco dei Daini numerosi sono gli esemplari distribuiti in maniera ordinata')
leads.why_not_published: 2026-08-07 verify pass. Described as numerous holm oaks planted in an ordered layout (deer park), i.e. a planted grove rather than an individual specimen. No single named tree found. Lead only.

blocked.name: Cedar of Lebanon of the San Sisto nursery
blocked.reason: Access restricted. The Semenzaio comunale di San Sisto Vecchio at Piazza di Porta Metronia 2 is a working municipal plant nursery that is not normally open to the public; it opens only for occasional booked guided visits run by the city. Publishing it would send people to a locked gate 280m from Villa Celimontana.

blocked.name: Ceiba of the San Sisto nursery
blocked.reason: Access restricted, same closed municipal nursery. Painful loss: 380cm, listed for size and botanical rarity, and Roma Capitale's own page calls it a tropical tree of splendid flowering.

blocked.name: American oak hybrid of the San Sisto nursery
blocked.reason: Access restricted, same closed municipal nursery.

blocked.name: Pomegranate of the Parco di San Sisto Vecchio
blocked.reason: Access restricted, same closed nursery grounds, and the register records 33 separate stems, so there is no single trunk to stand at.

blocked.name: Stone pine of Villa Torlonia, Viale Tiziano Terzani
blocked.reason: DEAD. On the Lazio register's removed sheet with the note 'Albero morto'. Recorded here so no future pass researches it from the national list, which still carries the entry.

blocked.name: Plane grove of the Parco di Porta Capena
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Registered as an 'insieme omogeneo', a homogeneous stand, with a group maximum girth instead of a trunk measurement. No single tree to stand in front of.

blocked.name: Oriental planes of the Fontane Oscure
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Group entry in Villa Borghese, 290m from the Valle dei Platani group that rom_002 already represents.

blocked.name: Oriental planes of the Valle dei Platani
blocked.reason: Group entry, and already represented: rom_002, Adonis, is the named individual within this stand. Kept here so the group is never shipped a second time as its own entry.

blocked.name: Ginkgos of Villa Sciarra
blocked.reason: Group entry, and already represented by rom_001. Note for the record: the register lists this as an 'insieme omogeneo' with a group maximum of 310cm, not as one tree, which is a caveat on how rom_001's girth figure is presented.

blocked.name: California fan palms of the Giardino Nicola Calipari
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Group of palms in the Piazza Vittorio garden, registered as a stand.

blocked.name: Fitolacca of Via Oletta
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point in the shape it is registered: five separate stems, listed for botanical rarity only, on a suburban street corner. Rome's ombu is already covered by rom_010 at the Cordonata.

blocked.name: Tenuta di Castelporziano, 22 registered trees
blocked.species: Quercus suber, Quercus robur, Quercus petraea, Quercus cerris, Alnus glutinosa and others
blocked.reason: Private and access-controlled. Castelporziano is the Presidential Estate, a working state property entered only on booked guided visits along fixed routes. A third of Rome's register sits inside it, including the 675cm cork oak that is the largest tree in the comune, and none of it can be published as a place someone walks to.

blocked.name: The most important Pine of the Pincio
blocked.reason: 2026-08-07 verify pass (rom deepen, Villa Borghese cluster). Amici di Villa Borghese's May 2024 open letter (carteinregola.it) describes it in the past tense as already felled: 'l'abbattimento di alberi storici al Pincio, compreso il Pino piu importante della Villa, candidato alla certificazione di albero monumentale d'Italia'. DEAD/GONE per this source. Recorded so no future pass researches this specific tree from scratch; it should not be confused with rom_016 (Coast Redwood of the Pincio), which is unrelated and still standing.
